extracted.intended_audience: general readers of short fiction / magazine readers interested in early-20th-century literary stories
extracted.subtask_description: A single short-story excerpt (early 20th-century magazine prose) containing narrative action and occasional meta-narratorial comments about storytelling craft (unity, atmosphere, use of hysteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of causation and climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The story elements together should present a complete unity of causation leading to a climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim context from the text: "the two presented the most complete possible unity of causation and climax. As a story, beyond which I have no interest, together they are admirable." (i.e., the linked episodes should show a coherent causal chain culminating in a satisfying climax.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of mood (atmosphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a consistent mood or atmosphere throughout, so that details of setting and surrounding color the reader's perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim context: "They were enveloped, too, in the consistency of mood loosely called atmosphere; that is, all the details of their surrounding combined to color the attentive mind with morbid shadows." (use of sensory/detail accumulation to sustain a particular atmosphere—here described as 'morbid shadows').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of abnormality/hysteria to illuminate character and deep emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ abnormal states (hysteria, uncanny events, the 'abnormal') as a means to reveal deep emotions, incentives, and aspects of human nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim context: "The abnormal often permits extraordinary glimpses of the human machine, ordinarily a sealed and impenetrable mystery. Hysteria has illuminated many of the deep emotions and incentives, and McGeorge... had the significant symptoms of that disturbance." (i.e., using hysterical or abnormal behavior can function as a device to expose inner motives and psychological truth.)
